actions.description: Move the bound MCS2 channel to an absolute position given in controller base units

inputs.description: Absolute target in controller base units: the position value this driver reads, whose physical value is position times 10**base_resolution of 'units'
inputs.name: position

actions.name: absolute_move

outputs.description: Position in base units read back after the move command was issued (the controller moves asynchronously)
outputs.name: position

actions.description: Move the bound MCS2 channel by a relative offset given in controller base units

inputs.description: Relative offset in controller base units (signed); the native move is relative to the current closed-loop position
inputs.name: offset

actions.name: relative_move

outputs.description: Position in base units read back after the move command was issued (the controller moves asynchronously)
outputs.name: position

actions.description: Start the reference search of the bound MCS2 channel (the native find_reference); the search itself is asynchronous
actions.name: find_reference

outputs.description: True once the reference command was issued
outputs.name: started

actions.description: Stop motion on the bound MCS2 channel (the native stop); the controller applies its configured stop profile and the call takes no profile
actions.name: stop_motion

outputs.description: True once the native stop call returned
outputs.name: stopped

facts.text: The wrapper's API is the SmarAct MCS2 Programmers Guide and the channel configuration (sensor type) is done beforehand with the SmarAct MCS2ServiceTool software
The base unit of a channel is generally a picometer for a linear positioner and a nanodegree for a rotary one
get_position reads the POSITION property of the channel and returns an int in base units; its docstring also describes the value as picometers
get_units returns the POS_BASE_UNIT enum name in lower case, or None when the base unit is BaseUnit.NONE
get_base_resolution returns the POS_BASE_RESOLUTION property as an integer exponent
get_positionner_type returns the POSITIONER_TYPE_NAME property of the channel
get_number_of_channels returns the controller's NUMBER_OF_CHANNELS; the docstring says it is not the number of connected positioners
absolute_move sets MOVE_MODE to CL_ABSOLUTE and calls Move with the value in base units
relative_move sets MOVE_MODE to CL_RELATIVE and calls Move with the value in base units
absolute_move and relative_move abort the movement without notice when a mechanical end stop is detected
find_reference starts the reference search in the forward direction and resets the position to zero if the configuration says so
stop calls Stop for the channel and also stops the hold position feature of closed-loop commands
The PyMoDAQ plugin converts a controller position to the plugin unit as 10**base_resolution times the position
The PyMoDAQ plugin applies the user-configured bounds with check_bound before an absolute move; the bound is a PyMoDAQ setting, not a controller limit
The MCS1 plugin's -61500 to 61500 um bounds correspond to one positioner, the SLC-24180
The MCS1 plugin comments that the minimum and maximum bounds depend on which positioner is plugged

measures.description: Current position of the bound channel in controller base units (multiply by 10**base_resolution for the value in the unit of 'units')
measures.name: position

measures.description: Base unit of the bound channel, or null when the channel reports BaseUnit.NONE
measures.name: units

measures.description: Base-resolution exponent of the bound channel: one base unit is 10**base_resolution of the unit reported by 'units'
measures.name: base_resolution

measures.description: Positioner type name reported by the bound channel
measures.name: positioner_type

measures.description: Number of channels the controller can handle (not the number of connected positioners)
measures.name: number_of_channels

measures.description: Controller channel this driver instance is bound to
measures.name: channel

operator_required.name: absolute_move
operator_required.reason: no text of the clone states the travel range of the positioner on an MCS2 channel: the base unit and resolution come from the configured positioner (generally a picometer for linear or a nanodegree for rotary). The only range in the clone is the MCS1 plugin's -61500 to 61500 um for one SLC-24180, and that plugin says the bounds depend on the plugged positioner. The operator supplies the range of the installed positioner in base units.
